div.l: No wondyr is he herd it alday
And ek ye knowen wel / that a Iay
Can clepe watte / as wel as the pope
But who so covde / in other thing hym grope
Than hadde he spent / al his philosophye
Ay questio que iuris / wold he crye
He was a Ientyl harlad / and a kynde
A bettyr felawe / shuld men nat fynde
He wolde suffre / for a quart of vyn ·
A good felawe / to have his concubyn
A twelve moneth / and excuse hym at the Fulle
Wel preuylych a fynch / cowde he pulle
And yif he fond owher / any good felawe
He wolde techen hym / to have noon awe
In such caas / of tharchedekenys curs
But of manys sowle / were in his purs
For in his purs / he shulde punched be
Purs is tharchedekenys helle seyde he
Of cursyng awhte / every man drede
And ther of tok the Sompnour / lytil hede
For curs wol sle / right as soylyng saveth
And also war hym / of a signyficauit
In daunger hadde he / at his owne gyse
The yonge gerlys / of the dyocyse
And knewe here conseil and was all here reed
A garland had he / set vp on his heed
As gret as it were / for an ale stake
A bokeler had he / made hym of a cake
WIth hym rood / a Ientil pardoner
Of Rouncivale / his frend and his comper
That streyht was come / from the court of Rome
Wel loved he song / come hedyr love to me .
